_comment: Spymaster registry config (docs/iteration-architecture.md step 2, codenames/spymasters/registry.py). Each entry names a Spymaster subclass (see SPYMASTER_CLASSES) and its constructor params. 'trained' marks whether this entry expects a trained artifact before it can be built -- true only for the clue policies, whose checkpoints come from their training scripts. 'roles' says which scripts pick an entry up without naming it: 'baseline' is the standard comparison set (both arenas), 'exploration' is only offered by scripts/pipeline/run_two_team_arena.py. A new entry omitting 'roles' defaults to ['baseline'], so it appears in the arenas automatically.

spymasters._comment: Clue search against the distilled listener (cache/listener_gbt.txt) scored by codenames/pl_reward.py, derived in docs/clue-selection-learned.tex. Two-stage: expected_words shortlists the clue pool with its Gaussian model (extract() is ~750us/clue, so scoring all 11,145 would be ~8.4s per turn), then the listener rescores the top `shortlist`. `sigma` tunes ONLY that shortlisting pass and has no effect on the final ranking -- it is set to 1.5 rather than the baseline's 2.5 because the sigma ladder found 1.5 the better value and the first stage's job is recall, not order. The listener is fitted to gpt-oss-120b, so evaluating against Sonnet is a transfer test, not a self-evaluation.
spymasters.name: learned_listener

spymasters._comment: The learned listener retrained with free-association counts (cache/listener_gbt_assoc_w0.3.txt), which give its scores an absolute level, plus a pass priced on that level: a fixed outside option at the score of a word named in `pass_rate` of association lists (codenames/spymasters/association_listener.py). pass_rate=null switches the pass off. Not swept; docs/versions/association_listener.md.
spymasters.name: association_listener

spymasters._comment: A clue policy (codenames/clue_policy.py): one network maps a board to pi(clue | board) over the incumbent's pool from raw clue-word evidence and roles, and an outcome head picks the number. These weights (cache/policy_imitation.pt) imitate the incumbent's picks and values on training boards; it is the control for gptoss_reward_policy, which starts from them. docs/versions/imitation_policy.md.
spymasters.name: imitation_policy

spymasters._comment: imitation_policy fine-tuned by REINFORCE on the reward gpt-oss-120b's guesses (temperature 1) earn on the policy's own clues, with a KL penalty to the imitation policy (scripts/pipeline/train_reward_policy.py, cache/policy_gptoss_reward.pt). docs/versions/gptoss_reward_policy.md.
spymasters.name: gptoss_reward_policy

spymasters._comment: A clue policy with a k head (no cap at 4). It imitates the uncapped incumbent's picks, then is trained by actor-critic on full games against learned_listener with gpt-oss-120b guessing. The only reward is the game's result, scored by a critic V(board) = P(win) learned from those games (scripts/pipeline/train_win_actor_critic.py, cache/win_policy.pt). Nothing reads the listener's probabilities. docs/versions/win_actor_critic.md.
spymasters.name: win_actor_critic

spymasters._comment: Reference opponent, not a model of ours: Claude Sonnet 5 shown the board with roles and asked for a clue (codenames/spymasters/llm_spymaster.py). Role 'reference' is picked up by no script automatically -- every game it plays costs money, so it is only ever run by name (scripts/pipeline/run_eval_suite.py learned_listener sonnet_spymaster).
spymasters.name: sonnet_spymaster
